past_trivia.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Canada has over 60% of Earth's lakes.

past_trivia.question: Holding roughly 20% of the Earth's unfrozen surface fresh water, what Siberian body of water is the deepest lake in the world?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Lake Baikal is also considered the world's oldest lake, estimated to be between 25 and 30 million years old.

past_trivia.question: Covering over 10,000 square kilometers, what famous landform in Bolivia holds the title of the world's largest salt flat?
past_trivia.fun_fact: During the rainy season, a thin layer of water transforms the flat into the world's largest natural mirror, so smooth it's used to calibrate satellite altimeters.

past_trivia.question: Which desert located primarily in northern Chile is widely recognized as the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: NASA uses the Atacama Desert to test instruments for Mars missions because its extreme dryness resembles Martian conditions.

past_trivia.question: Due to the Earth's equatorial bulge, which Ecuadorian volcano's summit is the farthest point from the center of the Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Because Earth bulges at the equator, Chimborazo's summit is over 6,800 feet farther from Earth's center than Everest, making it the closest point on Earth to the Moon.

past_trivia.question: Which African nation is the only independent country in the world situated entirely above 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) in elevation?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Known as the 'Kingdom of the Sky,' Lesotho is the only nation on Earth to lie entirely above 1,000 meters and contains Africa's highest pub at 2,874 meters.

past_trivia.question: Which country is home to Sossusvlei, a salt and clay pan surrounded by high red dunes located in the world's oldest desert?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Sossusvlei is part of the Namib Desert, which has existed for at least 55 million years, making it the oldest desert in the world.

past_trivia.question: Which geological depression in Ethiopia is widely considered one of the hottest, driest, and lowest places on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: Its colorful hydrothermal pools are created by sulfur, salt deposits, and acid-loving extremophile microbes thriving in extreme heat.

past_trivia.question: Which Icelandic volcano erupted in 2010, creating an ash cloud that grounded over 100,000 flights across Europe?
past_trivia.fun_fact: The 2010 eruption affected over 10 million passengers and was the largest disruption to air travel since World War II.

past_trivia.question: Bordered by Jordan, Israel, and the West Bank, what lake's surface sits at the lowest land-based elevation on Earth?
past_trivia.fun_fact: At around 430 meters below sea level, the Dead Sea is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean, making swimming feel like floating effortlessly.

past_trivia.question: Which village in the Meghalaya state of India is officially recognized as the wettest place on Earth, receiving an average annual rainfall of over 11,800 millimeters?
past_trivia.fun_fact: To work outdoors during heavy monsoons, locals in Mawsynram wear full-body, turtle-shell-shaped umbrellas called 'knups' made from bamboo and banana leaves.
